storage: Keep refrigerated, upright. Freezing cream splits it, so freeze only if it will be cooked into a sauce later.
looksLike: A thick, white to pale-cream pourable liquid sold in chilled cartons (tetra packs); it whips when cold.
howToPick: Cold, sealed carton, within date, no bulging. Cream that smells sour, has lumps or has separated is spoiled.
shelfLife: A chilled carton usually carries a few weeks (check the pack); open cream within about 2 to 3 days (general guidance).
substitutes: Homemade malai (cream skimmed from boiled full-cream milk)
Whisked thick curd added off the heat
Cashew paste (soaked, blended) or coconut cream
Thick curd/Greek yoghurt with a little milk

usedIn.raw: 20 ml (about 20 g) per serving (4 tsp; fresh cream about 25% fat, e.g. Amul fresh cream)
